subject: Recap + action plan: NextGen Health LLM offramp discovery
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Camille Torres <camille.torres@nextgenhealth.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@nextgenhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-18T22:05:00Z
Subject: Recap + action plan: NextGen Health LLM offramp discovery

Camille / Michael — thanks again for taking time today. Below is a short recap of what we heard on the call and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag any errors or missing context.

Summary of pain + goals
- Pain: Current dependency on proprietary APIs (OpenAI + Anthropic) is driving high cost (peaked at ~$120k/mo), unpredictable throttling during spikes, and limits on model-hosting options for regulated data.
- Goal: Move inference to an open-model stack (on-cloud or private) that preserves current prompt behaviors, keeps latency under 300ms p95 for the customer-facing chat API, and caps monthly inference spend below $60k.

Current stack (as described)
- Frontend: NextGen public chat and triage UI, calls our gateway.
- API layer: Proxies to OpenAI (gpt-4.1) for generation and Anthropic for safety/rerank; retries + fan-out logic for multimodel scoring.
- Logging/monitoring: Datadog for metrics, S3 for prompt+response logs (retention 90 days).
- Auth/data: Tokens scoped per tenant; PHI routed through a private VPC endpoint.

Success criteria (what you said matters)
- Functional parity on the top 20 prompts (measured BLEU/ROUGE-ish + human spot checks).
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for standard chat workloads (seq_len ~512).
- Cost target: ~<=50% of current API TCO (target <$60k/mo).
- Security/compliance: Ability to run in a VPC/on-premise and integrate with your KMS for keys.

Preliminary compatibility notes (from our side)
- Models to shortlist: Llama 3 family (30B quantized), Mistral Instruct variants, and RedPajama-INCITE-style tuned checkpoints. We’ll validate output parity vs. your top prompts.
- Gaps: Anthropic-specific safety chains (constitutional prompting + safety classifier) will need a migration plan — either re-implement internal classifiers or keep Anthropic for safety scoring as a fallback.

Action items (owners / ETA)
1) NextGen: Share sample prompt set + 20 canonical conversations (redacted of PHI) — Camille / Michael — by Jan 21.
2) Redwood SRE (Ben): Provide a short compatibility matrix (model latency estimates on gpus we recommend) and a first-pass cost model — Jan 25.
3) Redwood Security (Monica): Share SOC2 summary + on-prem checklist and proposed KMS integration options — Jan 22. (attaching SOC2 summary + compatibility matrix draft)
4) Joint: 30 min technical sync (deep-dive on retry/fanout behavior) — propose Jan 26 or 27.

Risks we flagged
- Prompt-engineered behaviors that rely on Anthropic response shaping may not reproduce 1:1 on open models.
- Data egress / PHI constraints for any managed hosted solution — may force Private deployment and increase infra ops work.

If that matches your read, we’ll put the compatibility matrix and the first-pass cost model in HubSpot and schedule the technical sync.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
